My thoughts on:You and Your Research. A speech by Richard Hemming

Aug 6, 2026 life

"The prepared mind sooner or later finds something important and does it." — Richard Hamming

This quote is very appealing to me because I think it says a lot in a few words. It speaks to people (like me) who do random things in an effort to be productive or whatever, not because I really want to and because it's a valuable thing to do, but just because I feel that I "should" do it. This is bad. What I hear in that quote is that if something isn't jumping out immediately to you of what you want to be doing in this moment, major or minor, then you need to take a step back. Instead of just mindlessly doing things for the sake of doing, start actually preparing for a moment of genuine interest hell yeah, by giving yourself freedom and space and exploring the things that you like so you are ready to jump into something when the time comes.
